tier_reason: Only first-party numbers: the README's enwik9 table (Core i7-6700) gives decompression times for lz4ultra 1.3.0 output vs lz4 1.9.2 -12 output, with no compiler, flags, decoder build or benchmark code.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table (enwik9, Core i7-6700): lz4ultra 1.3.0 --favor-decSpeed output (376,118,079 bytes) decompresses in 296,972 microseconds versus 457,141 microseconds for lz4 1.9.2 -12 --favor-decSpeed output (377,175,400 bytes), 1.54x faster (derived from page data); favor-ratio output 347,936 versus 505,804 microseconds (1.45x, derived) with 371,680,323 versus 372,443,347 compressed bytes (lz4ultra versus lz4).
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers, one dataset, no compiler flags, and the README does not say which decoder produced the timings (it says files are meant to be decompressed with lz4 and that its own decompressor is not as optimized as lz4 proper). Compared against lz4 1.9.2 (2019), not the current 1.10.0. smalLZ4 1.5 -9 in the same table is essentially identical in favor-ratio mode (371,680,328 bytes, 348,018 microseconds). Last commit 2023-01-29, more than 3 years ago. CC0 matchfinder carries no patent grant; it bundles libdivsufsort (MIT).

notes: Numbers match; the favor-ratio byte counts in claimed_speedup were in the wrong order and are fixed. lz4ultra is an independent optimal encoder producing standard LZ4 streams, not a fork, port or wrapper of lz4/lz4 (on the known list), so it does not fold; it is a complementary encoder for lz4's decoder. Zlib license (src/matchfinder.c CC0) confirmed from LICENSE; 62 stars.

tier_reason: The README makes only a directional claim ('designed to compare favorably against zlib's ratio and speed' at levels 2-9) with no numbers; the only independent numbers found (Wuffs doc/benchmarks.md, Core i5-10210U, Debian packages, gcc 10.2.1 / clang 11) show miniz 2.2.0 decoding SLOWER than zlib 1.2.11: 0.82-0.87x for raw deflate and 0.84-0.88x for zlib streams.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'at levels 2-9, miniz.c is designed to compare favorably against zlib's ratio and speed'; at level 1 it 'compresses around 5-9% better than minilzo, but is approx. 35% slower'. No numbers against zlib in the README. Independent Wuffs benchmarks (Core i5-10210U, Debian Bullseye builds) show miniz 2.2.0 decoding slower than zlib 1.2.11: deflate 10k 252 vs 289 MB/s (0.87x), 100k 287 vs 352 MB/s (0.82x); zlib 100k 272 vs 323 MB/s (0.84x). Compression speed versus zlib is unmeasured.
corrections.caveats: Not faster than zlib on any measured axis: Wuffs shows decompression at 0.82-0.88x of zlib 1.2.11, and the README's compression claim has no numbers. Its value is a single-file, MIT-licensed, zlib-API-compatible implementation with ZIP and PNG helpers, not speed. zlib-ng and libdeflate are much faster. Notable (2.9k stars, vcpkg port).

notes: Reject as not-faster on valid evidence, so under the keep-and-document rule the orchestrator may override to keep with the shortcoming above (it is notable, 2.9k stars). Metadata confirmed: MIT, 2.9k stars, last commit 2026-07-01, not archived. The README's 'miniz performance comparison page' link target was not located.
